title: Quick check: React Server Components

questions.prompt: In the context of “React Server Components” and “Server Components as the App Router default”, In the App Router, which component type is the default?
options: A Client Component with every page marked `use client`.
questions.explanation: Server Components are the default in the App Router; the client boundary is introduced where browser interactivity is needed.

lesson_context.focus: Server Components as the App Router default

questions.prompt: While implementing “React Server Components”, When is the `use client` directive appropriate?
options: For every static heading, regardless of need.
To make server-only credentials safe to expose publicly.
At the boundary of UI that needs state, event handlers, or browser-only APIs.
To allow a Server Component to directly use browser storage during server render.
questions.answer_key: At the boundary of UI that needs state, event handlers, or browser-only APIs.
questions.explanation: Use Client Components for interactivity and browser APIs; the directive does not make secrets safe for the browser.

lesson_context.focus: Server Components as the App Router default

questions.prompt: When reviewing “React Server Components”, How can a page reduce unnecessary client JavaScript?
options: Keep data loading and static composition on the server and isolate interactive elements in smaller Client Components.
Mark the root of the application as a Client Component by default.
Move all database queries into the browser.
Duplicate every component to force hydration.
questions.answer_key: Keep data loading and static composition on the server and isolate interactive elements in smaller Client Components.
questions.explanation: Deliberate server/client boundaries reduce bundle cost and clarify where code executes.

lesson_context.focus: Server Components as the App Router default
